1  HON'BLE PADAM NARAIN MISHRA, J. 
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants as well as learned AGA for the state.

2. This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants to quash the entire proceedings of Complaint Case No. 33 of 2014 (Ashutosh Singh vs. Madhukar Srivastava and Others), under Sections 406, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C., pending in the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 19, Deoria as well as summoning order dated 03.02.2014 passed in the aforesaid complaint case.
3.

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that all the disputes and differences have been settled between the parties byway of Settlement Agreement dated 21.12.2022 before the Mediation Centre, New Delhi District, Patiala House Court, New Delhi.
At this stage, learned counsel further submitted that continuation of the proceedings of the aforesaid case will be an abuse of process of law.
No fruitful purpose would be served by keeping the matter pending.

In support of his contention, learned counsel for the applicant has also placed reliance on the law laid down by Apex Court in Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab, (2012), 10 SCC 303, B.S. Joshi and others vs. State of Haryana and another, (2003) 4 SCC 675 and Madan Mohan Abbot vs. State of Punjab, (2008) 4 SCC 582.
5.

In Parbathbhai Aahir @ Parbatbhai Bhimsinghbhai Karmur & Others v. State of Gujarat &
another, (2017) 9 SCC 641, after referring the various precedents on the subject, summarized the broad principles relating to the inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Code as under:-
"16.4.

entities.text:
Parbathbhai Aahir @ Parbatbhai Bhimsinghbhai Karmur & Others v. State of Gujarat &
another, (2017) 9 SCC 641
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: While the inherent poser of the High Court has a wide ambit and plenitude it has to be exercised (i) to secure the ends of justice, or (ii) to prevent an abuse of the process of any court.

16.5. The decision as to whether a complaint or first information report should be quashed on the ground that the offender and victim have settled the dispute, revolves ultimately on the facts and circumstances of each case and no exhaustive elaboration of principles can be formulated."
6.
On the other hand, learned AGA has no objection if the proceedings of the aforesaid case pending before the trial court is quashed.
7. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record.

8. In all the aforesaid cases, the Apex Court has laid down the law that criminal proceedings may be quashed even in non-compoundable cases by the High Court in exercise of its extraordinary jurisdiction to restore peace between the parties and in case the justice so demands.

According to Hon'ble Supreme Court, if the offence involve private dispute between the parties of commercial Madhukar Srivastava And 4 Ors vs State Of U.P. And Another on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165782069/
2 nature or matrimonial dispute and it is not related to heinous offence, the proceedings may be quashed.

sentences.text: 9. The facts and circumstances as stated hereinabove are peculiar in the present case.
From perusal of the record, it is apparent that the offence is not of serious nature as the matter relates to offence under Sections 406, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C.
As such, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, no mental depravity is involved in the case.
If the request of the parties is denied, it will be amounting to only adding one more criminal case to the already overburdened criminal courts.

10. Since the dispute between the parties has been amicably and mutually settled, no fruitful purpose would be served by permitting to continue the criminal case pending before the trial court and it would simply be a waste of time if the aforesaid case is permitted to continue till its logical conclusion.
11. In view of the above, the Application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. is allowed.

12. The entire proceedings of entire proceedings of Complaint Case No. 33 of 2014 (Ashutosh Singh vs. Madhukar Srivastava and Others), under Sections 406, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C., pending in the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 19, Deoria as well as summoning order dated 03.02.2014, against the applicants are quashed in terms of compromise arrived at between the parties.
